applicationPool.reason: the only pool entry that is simultaneously a real React Native application with a checked-in root ios/ project, reachable with no account and no hosted service, and buildable for the simulator without a signing identity. Containment is required on four points: the app target embeds a watch app, a widgets extension and a stickers extension, which must be stripped from the campaign scheme; ios/BlueWallet/BlueWallet.entitlements requests aps-environment, an application group and the camera, which are inert only because an unsigned simulator build embeds no entitlements; older revisions hardcode DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = A7W54YZ4WU in four build configurations, so the build recipe must force it empty rather than assume it is unset; and Electrum network access must be blocked, which restricts selection to defects whose trigger is local
applicationPool.candidateDefectsBasis: GitHub search reports 178 merged pull requests in this repository whose body contains "closes #". The offline, simulator-triggerable subset is far smaller; five pairs are verified below and several more were verified and then set aside for camera or network dependence

selectedDefects.issueTitle: "tools->is it my address?" fails if bech32 address is ALL CAPS
selectedDefects.frameworkEvidence: React Native verified at the affected revision: git show 2dfb59e3:package.json reports dependencies.react-native = 0.77.2, and git ls-tree lists 26 entries under ios/ including BlueWallet.xcodeproj, BlueWallet.xcworkspace and Podfile. The fix commit is a squash whose sole parent is the affected revision

simulatorBuildWithoutSigning.evidence: at this revision all eight DEVELOPMENT_TEAM occurrences in project.pbxproj are empty, CODE_SIGN_STYLE is Manual with an empty PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER, and CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY is set only for [sdk=iphoneos*], [sdk=macosx*] and [sdk=watchos*], so the simulator configuration inherits no identity. The aps-environment and application-group entitlements are never embedded when signing is disabled

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is Tools, then is it my address, typing an all-caps bech32 address into a React Native TextInput and pressing check. Text entered through XCUITest travels native keyboard to RCTUITextField to the Hermes side through onChangeText, is normalized by the wallet-matching logic there, and the result is rendered back into a native text view. That is exactly the react-native-ios adapter's full loop: the iOS text input surface plus the JS engine, and the defect is a casing normalization bug, so the precise bytes crossing the bridge decide the outcome. Fully offline: address matching is local
remaining: build the affected and fixed revisions for the simulator with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO and a scheme that excludes the watch, widgets and stickers targets, and record the exact command and result
prove the Appium XCUITest session can reach the tools screen with the network blocked
state the exact identity and authority for the observable, and minimize the trigger
run three affected reproductions and three fixed controls on a reset simulator with reset evidence
record neighboring legal behavior: the same address in lowercase must still match on the affected build

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Unable to delete multiple wallets without restarting the app
selectedDefects.frameworkEvidence: React Native verified at the affected revision: git show 5c80b856:package.json reports dependencies.react-native = 0.77.2, and git ls-tree lists 26 entries under ios/. The fix commit is a squash whose sole parent is the affected revision

simulatorBuildWithoutSigning.evidence: same 0.77.2 era project as the uppercase bech32 candidate: eight empty DEVELOPMENT_TEAM settings and device-scoped CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY only

selectedDefects.whySuitable: this is the strongest adapter-level candidate in the set. The bug lives in the navigation stack: after the first wallet is deleted, an imperative popToTop leaves the native UINavigationController managed by react-native-screens out of sync with the JS navigation state, so the second delete does nothing until relaunch. Reproducing it needs a real multi-step XCUITest session that creates two wallets, enters details, deletes, re-enters and deletes again, and the failure is visible only as a native screen that does not pop. No pure-JS harness can observe it, so it separates this target from a Hermes-only oracle. Entirely offline
remaining: build both revisions for the simulator with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO

blockers.detail: all five verified candidates come from a single application, BlueWallet. It is the only repository in the pool that is a real React Native application with a checked-in root ios/, reachable without an account or hosted service, and buildable unsigned for the simulator. The field benchmark requires two independent applications, so a second qualifying application must be found or the monorepo sub-application rule must be extended to admit WordPress/gutenberg packages/react-native-editor

no candidate has been built. Every simulatorBuildWithoutSigning entry is an inspection of project.pbxproj and the entitlements file at the affected revision, not an executed xcodebuild, so buildQualified is null for the whole pool

the affected revisions span React Native 0.72.14 through 0.85.3, so no single CocoaPods and Xcode recipe is known to build all of them. The 0.72 candidate is the most likely to fail toolchain resolution on the current host
